hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find the normal contact force: $R = 5g\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
The block slides up the plane, so limiting friction acts down the plane: $F = \mu R = 25\sqrt{3}\mu$.
Set the net force acting up the plane to be positive: $40 - 5g\sin 30^\circ - F > 0$, and solve the inequality for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane to find normal reaction $R$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 5g\cos 30^\circ = 5(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Since the block begins to slide up the plane, the limiting friction force acts down the plane:
$$F = \mu R = 25\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Set the net force up the plane to be strictly greater than zero (or acceleration $a > 0$):
$$40 - 5g\sin 30^\circ - F > 0$$
$$40 - 5(10)(0.5) - 25\sqrt{3}\mu > 0$$
$$40 - 25 - 25\sqrt{3}\mu > 0$$
$$15 > 25\sqrt{3}\mu$$
$$\mu < \frac{15}{25\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3}{5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5} = \frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve forces acting on the $5\text{ kg}$ block perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ$$
Substitute $m = 5\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 5 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

When the block begins to slide up the plane, limiting friction opposes the upward motion and acts down the plane:
$$F = \mu R = 25\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Apply Newton's second law up the inclined plane:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$40 - mg\sin 30^\circ - F = 5a$$
Substitute the known values:
$$40 - 5(10)(0.5) - 25\sqrt{3}\mu = 5a$$
$$40 - 25 - 25\sqrt{3}\mu = 5a$$
$$15 - 25\sqrt{3}\mu = 5a$$

For the block to slide up the plane, the acceleration must be positive ($a > 0$), or equivalently the net force must exceed zero:
$$15 - 25\sqrt{3}\mu > 0$$
$$25\sqrt{3}\mu < 15$$
Divide both sides by $25\sqrt{3}$:
$$\mu < \frac{15}{25\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3}{5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5} = \frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}$$

hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane, noting that the horizontal $40\text{ N}$ force pushes into the incline: $R = 5g\cos 30^\circ + 40\sin 30^\circ$.

Resolve forces parallel to the plane: component of $40\text{ N}$ up the plane is $40\cos 30^\circ \approx 34.6\text{ N}$, which exceeds component of weight down the plane ($5g\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$). Thus friction acts down the plane: $F = 40\cos 30^\circ - 25$.
For equilibrium without slipping, $F \le \mu R$. Set $\mu \ge \frac{F}{R}$ to find the least possible value.
walkthrough:
Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find normal reaction $R$:
$$R = 5g\cos 30^\circ + 40\sin 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3} + 40(0.5) = 20 + 25\sqrt{3} \approx 63.3013\text{ N}$$

Resolve parallel to the plane. Since $40\cos 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64\text{ N} > 5g\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$, friction $F$ acts down the plane to prevent motion:
$$F = 40\cos 30^\circ - 5g\sin 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} - 25 \approx 9.6410\text{ N}$$

Apply the condition for equilibrium $F \le \mu R$:
$$\mu \ge \frac{F}{R} = \frac{20\sqrt{3} - 25}{20 + 25\sqrt{3}} = \frac{9.6410}{63.3013} \approx 0.1523$$

State the least possible value of $\mu$ correct to 3 decimal places:
$$\mu_{\text{min}} = 0.152$$
teacher_walkthrough: In Fig. 6.2, the force of magnitude $40\text{ N}$ acts horizontally towards the incline.

Resolve perpendicular to the incline (taking outward normal as positive):
The weight has component $mg\cos 30^\circ$ into the incline.
The horizontal force pushes into the incline at angle $30^\circ$ to the slope, contributing $40\sin 30^\circ$ into the surface.
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ + 40\sin 30^\circ$$
Substitute $m = 5\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$:
$$R = 5(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 40(0.5) = 25\sqrt{3} + 20 \approx 63.3013\text{ N}$$

Resolve parallel to the incline to determine the direction of the friction force:
The horizontal force pushes up the incline with component $40\cos 30^\circ = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64\text{ N}$.
The weight pulls down the incline with component $mg\sin 30^\circ = 5(10)(0.5) = 25\text{ N}$.
Because the upward component ($34.64\text{ N}$) is greater than the downward component ($25\text{ N}$), the block tends to slide up the plane. Hence, friction $F$ must act downwards along the plane to maintain equilibrium:
$$F + mg\sin 30^\circ = 40\cos 30^\circ$$
$$F = 40\cos 30^\circ - 5g\sin 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} - 25 \approx 9.6410\text{ N}$$

State the equilibrium condition preventing sliding:
$$F \le \mu R$$
Substitute the calculated values:
$$9.6410 \le \mu \times 63.3013$$
Divide by $63.3013$:
$$\mu \ge \frac{9.6410}{63.3013} \approx 0.1523$$

Conclude that the least possible value to 3 decimal places is:
$$\mu_{\text{min}} = 0.152$$
